page: Amazon Web Services c6gd.2xlarge is a compute-optimized server powered by an AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 processor. Built on the 64-bit ARMv8 architecture, this instance provides 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs operating at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz with no hyperthreading. It features 16.0 GB of system memory, translating to 2.0 GB per core, and includes 474 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage. The server runs on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals average multi-core performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 12133.14 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 5364.0. The server demonstrates solid capabilities in software compilation with a Geekbench clang score of 8140.0 and database operations with a Passmark database score of 5269.76. Redis SET operations reach 9.43 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput is measured at 9.78 GB/sec. However, single-core performance is relatively weak, as shown by a Geekbench single-core score of 930.0 and a single-threaded bzip3 decompression speed of 6.93 GB/sec.

The c6gd.2xlarge offers a balanced profile for compute-heavy workloads that benefit from local NVMe storage, such as distributed databases, caching layers, and web serving. The lack of x86 instruction sets and lower single-core performance are key tradeoffs to consider. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ARM-based Graviton architecture provides a resource-dense compute platform with dedicated physical cores, making it highly suitable for multi-threaded applications, microservices, and containerized deployments that do not require GPU acceleration.
